dependency_evidence: Yoder et al. describe Joshua tree-yucca moth interaction as classic obligate mutualism; female moths oviposit in flowers and larvae consume yucca seeds, and western Joshua tree populations are associated with T. synthetica
witness_selection_rule: Use the 14 Table-1 Tegeticula synthetica western sites only. Each admitted site has a positive moth microsatellite or moth ovipositor sample. Exclude all three Tikaboo contact-zone sites because host specificity is explicitly relaxed there, and exclude all eastern T. antithetica sites.
host_range_evidence: USDA Forest Service FEIS: western Joshua tree occurs on 1,788,371 ha in California and Nevada; this stable non-occurrence range authority satisfies the prospective >=2-region host breadth screen
known_boundary: JOS001 is the first v7.1 engineering pilot and is permanently firewalled from the later confirmatory endpoint. Passing any downstream gate is engineering feasibility, not confirmation of the invariant.
